paper_metadata.title: Hierarchical microstructure strengthening in a single crystal high entropy superalloy

evidence.quote: A hierarchical microstructure strengthened high entropy superalloy (HESA) with superior cost specific yield strength from room temperature up to 1,023 K is presented.
The HESA of interest is Ni48.3Co16.9Al10.2Fe8.9Cr7.4Ti5.8Nb1.2Mo0.9W0.4 (at.%)27.

other.description: HT-1: single ramp from room temperature to 1,500 K in 20 h followed by air cooling

evidence.quote: HT-1 consisted a single ramp from room temperature to 1,500 K in 20 h followed by air cooling, and the microstructure contained cuboidal precipitates and nano-particles, Fig. 1a

other.description: HT-2: additional heat treatment at 1,023 K for 20 h followed by water quenching

evidence.quote: After an additional heat treatment at 1,023 K for 20 h followed by water quenching, the HT-2 process caused the L12 phase to grow from 143 to 153 nm in average and secondary L12 particles to coarsen into an average of 14 nm as shown in Fig. 1c
These single crystal bars were cast by Bridgman process. Laue X-ray method was used to make sure the < 100 > orientation of each single crystal bar.

the as-cast single crystal bars were solution heat treated by a single ramp process from room temperature to 1,500 K in 20 h and air cooled to room temperature (this heat treatment process is termed HT-1).
After HT-1 process, an additional heat treatment was performed at 1,023 K for 20 h followed by water quench (the entire heat treatment process is termed HT-2).
To further examine the microstructure evolution of HESA, a prolonged ageing after HT-1 was done at 1,023 K up to 200 h followed by water quench.
In the HT-1 condition, HESA possessed a High Entropy (HE) FCC matrix and Medium Entropy (ME) precipitates (L12).
The precipitation of L12 phase (143 nm in size) and secondary L12 particles (1 nm in size) occurred during the air cooling process in HT-1
the HT-2 process caused the L12 phase to grow from 143 to 153 nm in average
these nano-particles could be determined indirectly as disordered FCC particles.
HESA is strengthened by an interesting hierarchical microstructure consisted of FCC matrix, L12 precipitates inside FCC matrix, and FCC particles inside L12 particles.
The HT-1 condition contained an average L12 phase size of 143 nm and the L12 phase volume fraction of 68.4%
the HT-2 condition possessed an average L12 phase size of 153 nm and the L12 phase volume fraction of 70.6%
the average HE-FCC particle radius and volume fraction were measured as r = 4 nm and f = 4.3%, respectively
HESA in HT-1 state could achieve a yield strength of 880 MPa at 298 K and 954 MPa at 1,023 K
HESA in HT-1 state could achieve a yield strength of 880 MPa at 298 K and 954 MPa at 1,023 K
HESA in the HT-2 state exhibited even higher yield strength (993 MPa at 298 K and 1,023 MPa at 1,023 K) comparing to those of the HT-1 state.
HESA in the HT-2 state exhibited even higher yield strength (993 MPa at 298 K and 1,023 MPa at 1,023 K) comparing to those of the HT-1 state.
The yield strength of HESA in the HT-2 state was 113 MPa higher than that of the HT-1 state.

the increase in yield strength due to nano HE-FCC particles is 110 MPa, which is almost the same as the actual yield strength increase determined by experiment, i.e. 113 MPa, from the HT-1 state to the HT-2 state.
at 1,023 K, the cost specific yield strength of HESA is 8 times that of CMSX-4 while its tensile strain can reach 20%, which is 3 times that of CMSX-4.
Therefore, the formation of FCC particles in HESA was driven by the supersaturation of FCC phase formers inside the L12 phase.
The dispersion of HE-FCC particles in ME-L12 precipitates can pin superdislocations, Fig. 5, attributing to an average increase of 113 MPa in yield strength comparing to that of the HT-1 condition.
